headline: Your Ottonomy waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing facility operators into the right Ottobot offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Divyansh Taya, Office of the CEO.
productSummary: Ottobots are Ottonomy's Level-4 autonomous delivery robots. They move medical supplies, parts, meals, and parcels across indoor corridors and outdoor campus ground, and they plug into the elevators and access doors the site already has. Ottumn.AI is the cloud orchestration layer for the fleet. Healthcare, large industrial campuses, and last-mile parcel. Sold as Robotics-as-a-Service. No infrastructure rip-out.
coreInsight: Divyansh already sells indoor-outdoor movement for jobs people should not be doing. The one TAM is facility operators Google Maps already lists as hospitals, campuses, airports, universities, and last-mile hubs. The one routing signal is how many of those Places sit under the same operator, because Maps returns that count in the same pull and it tells you whether they run a network, a multi-building campus, a two-building A-to-B run, or a single site still walking it.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how many sites Maps already lists
sections.takeaway: Google Maps already names the hospital, campus, airport, or last-mile hub, and it already groups those Places under one operator. That location count is stronger than a headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every facility operator
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Ten-plus site networks go first, then multi-building campuses, then two-building A-to-B pairs, then every remaining in-TAM Place.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each campus count gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Networks get a multi-site movement teardown. Campuses get an indoor-outdoor brief. Pairs get an A-to-B pilot map. The rest get a workforce-gap pilot one-pager.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Save time, save money, stop the walking, on the same routes
sections.takeaway: The list is always Maps facility operators, aimed at ops, nursing, facilities, and last-mile leads. Industry is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the campus Maps already shows
sections.takeaway: Notice the site count, poke the human run that count implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the multi-site network first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already move things across 10+ facilities. Prove reply density, then roll campus, pair-run, and the workforce-gap catch-all.

signalReasons: Google Maps categories for hospital, campus, airport, university, and last-mile hub are the TAM Ottonomy's three industry pages already sell into, in one pull.
The same pull groups Places by brand or website, which is enough to route on location_count without a second enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Ottonomy copy: Ottumn.AI for fleets, indoor-outdoor plus elevator/door V2X for campuses, the floor-two-to-lab run for pairs, and RaaS plus workforce-gap language for everyone else.
Healthcare, industrial campus, and parcel are a scrape filter. They are not a second waterfall.

sources.name: Google Maps Places
sources.delivers: Hospital, medical campus, industrial campus, airport, university, last-mile hub, hotel, and residential campus operators. The TAM gate and the spine of every route. One pull.

sources.name: Google Maps brand / domain grouping
sources.delivers: location_count, the integer used to assign Tier 1 / 2 / 3 / catch-all

sources.name: Related-POI campus cluster
sources.delivers: Hidden multi-building campuses when a single hospital Place sits next to lab, pharmacy, and parking Places

sources.name: Company locations page scrape
sources.delivers: Backup location_count when Maps under-counts a health system or industrial group

sources.name: LinkedIn Sales Navigator
sources.delivers: Ops, CNO, materials management, facilities, last-mile, and airport-innovation titles after the operator is routed

sources.name: Apollo (after qualification)
sources.delivers: Work emails for already-routed accounts. Do not buy a raw robotics list and hope.

sources.name: Optional customer suppress
sources.delivers: Named on-site deployments (Wellstar, CVG, PIT, Munich, AdR, Posten Norge, Sodexo, Harbor Lockers). Thin coverage. Treat as a suppress list, not a tier.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Multi-site network
tiers.trigger: Google Maps groups 10+ Places under one operator: health system, university system, industrial group, airport group, or postal / locker network
tiers.pain: They already run a logistics network between sites. Human runners, vans, and shift rosters do not scale with site count. Parking and time show up as soon as vans try to serve a dense cluster.
tiers.valueProp: Ottumn.AI orchestrates modular robots and smart infrastructure across healthcare, industrial, and urban environments. 24/7, no shift cap. Homepage: last mile is over 50% of total shipping costs. Footer: RaaS versus traditional 3rd-party delivery.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already move things across a network of sites.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Multi-building campus
tiers.trigger: 3-9 mapped buildings or related POIs, and not already a 10+ network
tiers.pain: Enough campus that indoor-outdoor is the job. Staff still walk long distances with parts, samples, trays, or mail between buildings, including in weather.
tiers.valueProp: L4 plus Contextual AI, seamless indoor-outdoor, V2X with elevators and access doors, zero infrastructure changes. Modular cabins. Unified campus network even across hundreds of acres and outdoor conditions.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. The campus is visible. The run is still done by people.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Indoor-outdoor pair
tiers.trigger: Exactly 2 mapped buildings: hospital+lab, plant+warehouse, kitchen+rooms, or mailroom+residential block
tiers.pain: The painful run is a known A-to-B: floor two, elevator, outdoor crossing, other building. That motion is already staffed by people.
tiers.valueProp: Ottobots take blood samples, meds, parts, or meals from collection point to destination, between floors via elevators and across buildings. Locked compartments, RFID/HID, chain of custody. Homepage: free up 40% of nursing time currently spent on non-clinical tasks.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. The pair proves the indoor-outdoor job Ottobot exists to take.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining TAM
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM Place: single-site hospital, plant, airport, university, last-mile hub, hotel, or residential campus
tiers.pain: They are still in the facility set Ottonomy sells into. Movement is still done by people. The homepage job is the one people cannot or should not do.
tiers.valueProp: RaaS, no infrastructure changes, 24/7, contactless. Healthcare: 40% of nursing time on non-clinical tasks. Parcel: last mile over 50% of shipping costs. Named voices already on the homepage.
tiers.dataSource: Maps TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

campaigns.name: Multi-Site Movement Teardown
campaigns.strategy: Name the Maps site count and contrast shift-roster movement with Ottumn.AI fleet orchestration that runs 24/7
campaigns.overview: Scrape Maps operators, write to the ops track, and lead with the network they already run that still depends on vans and walkers.

campaigns.name: Last-mile cost variant
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 1 list, cost copy instead of roster copy
campaigns.strategy: Keep the site count in the notice line. Swap the poke to last mile as over 50% of shipping costs and RaaS versus 3rd-party vans.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the teardown. Same exclusive route, cost language instead of shift language.

campaigns.name: Indoor-Outdoor Campus Brief
campaigns.strategy: Name the campus buildings Maps shows, then offer elevator/door V2X and indoor-outdoor L4
campaigns.overview: The classic campus majority. Indoor-outdoor side of the A/B.

campaigns.name: All-weather 24/7 variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep the building count in the first line. Lead with 24/7 all-weather and hundreds of acres.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the campus brief. Same waterfall tier, weather-and-shifts hook.

campaigns.name: Pair-Run Pilot Map
campaigns.strategy: Name the two Places and the A-to-B run, then offer the elevator-and-outdoor motion with 40% nursing time when facility_type is hospital
campaigns.overview: The two-building majority. A-to-B side of the A/B.

campaigns.name: Chain-of-custody variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep the two buildings in the first line. Lead with locked compartments, RFID/HID, and chain of custody.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the pilot map. Same exclusive route, custody language.

campaigns.name: Workforce-Gap Pilot One-Pager
campaigns.strategy: Notice the facility Maps already lists, name the job people should not be doing, offer a RaaS pilot one-pager
campaigns.overview: Catch-all coverage so every scraped facility still gets one route. One-pager is the tiny yes.

campaigns.name: No-infra-change starter
campaigns.strategy: Lead with zero infrastructure changes and elevator/door integration. Do not change routing.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the one-pager. Still exclusive catch-all, still one TAM.

launchPlan: Pull Google Maps Places for hospital, campus, airport, university, industrial, last-mile, hotel, and residential categories in US, UK, EU, Australia, and India. Group by website domain or brand. Keep location_count, named_site, facility_type, review_count, and open_24h in the same export. Suppress already_customer when a named deployment is visible.
Resolve ops, CNO, facilities, last-mile, and airport-innovation titles only after the operator is routed. Apollo last.
Launch Tier 1 Multi-Site Movement Teardown first. Smallest list, sharpest network signal. Save-time copy as the control, last-mile cost as the A/B on the same list.
Add Tier 2 Indoor-Outdoor Campus Brief once related-POI clustering is clean. Then Tier 3 Pair-Run Pilot Map.

Turn on the Workforce-Gap Pilot One-Pager catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM Place still has a route. Keep facility_type as a merge tag, not a campaign split, until one campus-count tier is clearly working.

thresholds.action: Perfect. Scale that tier. Keep the winning time, cost, or custody variant.
Good. Let it run. Do not mix a non-facility TAM into this waterfall.
Borderline. Swap only the magnet or the first-line site name. Do not change the route.

thresholds.rate: Worse than 1 per 500, or reply rate under 1% after 1,500+ sends
thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall.
